Title: Dengkil pupil's death: Education Ministry offers support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is providing psychosocial support to the family and school community of a Year One pupil who died after experiencing breathing difficulties in her classroom in Dengkil.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the ministry would leave the investigation to the police, with its immediate focus on supporting the family and school community.
"We extend our condolences to the family. The ministry has taken steps to provide psychosocial support to the family and the school community," she told reporters after attending the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 Literacy Programme at the Malaysian Teacher Education Institute's Malay Language Campus today.
She said the ministry would be guided by the findings of the police investigation.
The pupil died yesterday after experiencing
breathing difficulties
in her classroom at a school in Dengkil.
On whether schools in the Klang Valley would close due to the haze, Fadhlina said the decision would be made jointly by the Education, Health and Environment ministries under the emergency action plan.
She said the Environment Ministry was monitoring the situation, while the Health Ministry would advise on the health risks.
The three ministries would consult one another before deciding whether schools should close or reopen, she added.
Fadhlina said the decision required a balance between protecting pupils' health and minimising disruption to learning.
"We hope the situation will not drag on. We know there are health risks if schools remain open, but prolonged closures also lead to learning loss.
"Both concerns require careful consideration and guidance before a decision is made," she said.
All schools in Selangor operated as usual today, although
outdoor activities
were suspended due to the haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police record 18 statements in MCBA officer's murder probe
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police have recorded statements from 18 people to assist investigations into the death of a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the deputy public prosecutor in the near future.
"The suspect, who is the victim's husband in his 30s, remains in remand until Oct 22 to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
"Checks also revealed that the man has 16 previous criminal and drug-related offences," he said.
Alzafny said the post-mortem found the victim died from pressure applied to her neck, alongside three stab wounds from a sharp weapon —two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.
The victim, who was in her 30s, was found dead after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband at the quarters following a reported misunderstanding.
Police received a report on the incident at 9.30pm after the husband turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Italy to send 500 troops to Milan after clashes
Article:
ROME: Italy is preparing to send 500 troops to Milan after looting and clashes between police and mostly young protesters, with some luxury brands shutting their shops in the city.
A cabinet meeting on Tuesday is expected to give the go-ahead to the deployment and approve policing powers for soldiers temporarily supporting law enforcement in the city.
Hundreds of protesters were detained during two days of clashes in Milan on Saturday and Sunday and dozens of police officers were injured.
Several shops in the fashion hub were looted. Some shops this week have remained closed or removed window displays and beefed up security.
More protests are expected on Saturday.
The government is also considering a wider crackdown, including restrictions on public gatherings, easing rules on detention for minors and harsher sanctions for their parents.
Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini called the clashes "shameful" and said on RTL 102.5 radio that the cabinet meeting would announce a series of "immediate measures" including the troop deployment.
Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said on Monday hoped the cabinet meeting would approve provisions for the army "to allow them to act like law enforcement."
Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Saturday said the violent perpetrators were "thugs who exploit demonstrations to spread chaos, attack those who guarantee security, and hold entire cities hostage."
"To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not," she wrote on X.
High school and university students, farmers and truck drivers are leading nationwide protests in Italy, mainly against the rising cost of living.
Hard-right leader Meloni faces elections next year in which the state of the economy, security and immigration are likely to be the key issues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN plans appeal, premature to comment on status, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It is premature to comment on Perikatan Nasional's status following its deregistration, as the coalition intends to appeal, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said questions on the matter should be directed to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, who oversees the Registrar of Societies.
"I think let them be, because now they want to file an appeal, right? I won't respond. In English, (it) says premature," she told reporters at a press conference during the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 Literacy Programme at the Malaysian Teacher Education Institute's Malay Language Campus today.
The
Registrar of Societies
today cancelled Perikatan Nasional's registration after finding that the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
Perikatan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today that the coalition would
challenge
the deregistration and seek a court stay of the decision.
The Registrar of Societies issued Perikatan Nasional a show-cause notice on Sept 22 and suspended its
activities
the following day, following a complaint by component party Bersatu.
The High Court on Oct 13 granted Perikatan Nasional leave to challenge the suspension, with its application for a stay to be heard on Thursday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel arrests 10 after West Bank settler attacks on US photographer, French mayor
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 people in the occupied West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government.
In a rare action against rising settler violence, police said they raided several locations across the occupied territory and seized cars and potential evidence related to the attacks.
"Following the severe incidents of violence over the past weekend, including the assault of a media worker and the suspected attacks on foreign civilians, an arrest operation was conducted before dawn," said Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police's West Bank commander.
"Suspects were arrested on suspicion of involvement in the violent incidents, violating a military commander's order concerning a closed military zone, and illegal construction," he said.
Witnesses say that settlers have been stepping up violent attacks on Palestinians during the ongoing olive harvest, aiming to seize their land during a season that carries cultural importance for the community.
Rights groups note that Israel rarely prosecutes settlers when the victims are Palestinian.
The Israeli human rights group Yesh Din said it documented 561 acts of settler or military violence against Palestinians since Sept 27 – more than 26 incidents a day.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is facing a tight race for a new mandate, has tried to shore up his pro-settlement right-wing base and has cast doubt on the circumstances behind the recent settler attacks on Westerners.
Netanyahu's tone has brought unusually strong criticism from the opposition, which has accused him of tarnishing Israel's image.
US ambassador Mike Huckabee, a staunch ally of Israel, had called Friday's beating of veteran photographer Heidi Levine an "act of terror" and demanded punishment. He called Monday's arrests a "very positive development."
Levine, 65, who was on assignment for The Washington Post, was taken to a hospital with broken vertebrae. From her hospital bed, she received a telephone call from President Isaac Herzog, who holds a largely ceremonial role, and was visited by centre-left opposition leader Yair Golan.
Golan in a social media post afterwards said that if he takes power, there will no longer be "a reality in which Jews instil terror in the name of Jewish supremacy, and stain the state we built here."
Palestinian officials and witnesses reported a series of new attacks even after the arrests, including an attempt by settlers to storm a school near olive groves and the shooting and wounding of a young man near Nablus.
- RISING INTERNATIONAL ATTENTION -
One day after Levine's beating, settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats including the French and Belgian consuls general in Jerusalem as they went through the town of Taybeh in the West Bank on Saturday.
The settlers beat up Bernard Baudoux, 78, the mayor of the northern French town of Aulnoye-Aymeries who was wearing a sash in the French tricolour during a goodwill visit in which he helped harvest olives.
Netanyahu earlier questioned the facts behind the two recent incidents.
On Levine's beating, he alleged that Palestinians and "far-left" activists were fanning violence. With the attack on the diplomatic convoy, he pointed out that the mayor was a leftist supporter of the Palestinian cause and said that diplomats should have coordinated with the Israeli military.
The top official on human rights in the US State Department, Riley Barnes, on Sunday visited the same town where the mayor was beaten, which is largely Christian, on a trip coordinated with the military. He was unharmed.
The violence by settlers has led British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband to accuse Israel of an "ethnic cleansing" campaign and for his government to impose sanctions on goods from settlements.
Marking Monday's deadline for Israel accepting construction tenders for the E1 settlements, a major new project that Palestinians fear will divide the West Bank in two, Miliband warned businesses about consequences.
"They should be aware of legal and reputational consequences, including the risk of involving themselves in serious breaches of international law," Miliband said in a statement.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar hit back against what he called an "obsession" with Israel by British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government.
"The days when Israel would quietly accept threats, sanctions and attempts to dictate its policies are over," Saar said.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MASFIH proposes nine priorities to help families of Malaysians missing in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) has proposed nine key priorities to address challenges faced by families of 54 Malaysians who remain missing following the Aug 26 Nepal-Tibet flood disaster.
The proposals include establishing a coordinated national response mechanism, seeking urgent legal clarification from the Attorney-General's Chambers, developing a legal framework for exceptional overseas mass-disappearance cases, and obtaining official confirmation of the missing persons' status.
MASFIH spokesperson Dr R. Manivannan said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today, alongside a 29-page document outlining recommended interventions, implementation priorities and coordinated government action.
"MASFIH appreciates the prime minister's attention to these concerns and the opportunity to convey the urgent needs of the affected families.
"We hope the meeting will lead to coordinated government action, clear responsibilities and practical measures to support all those affected," he said at Parliament today.
Manivannan said Anwar would discuss the matter at Friday's Cabinet meeting, including the appointment of a minister to coordinate the government's response.
He said MASFIH was also seeking official letters confirming that the individuals were missing, rather than merely uncontactable, to enable their families to apply for financial moratoriums.
The 54 Malaysians remain missing as their families continue seeking reliable information and assistance to navigate the financial, legal and administrative difficulties arising from the prolonged uncertainty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan exco removals: Govt explanation still under discussion, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's response to calls for an explanation of the constitutional basis for the removal of 10 Negri Sembilan executive council (exco) members is still under discussion, says Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the relevant ministry might address the matter during the winding-up of the debate in the Dewan Rakyat.
"The discussion is not over yet. Many people want to say all sorts of things.
"Later, during the winding-up, perhaps whichever ministry is relevant will wind up," she told reporters at a press conference held in conjunction with the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 Literacy Programme at the Malaysian Teacher Education Institute's Malay Language Campus today.
She was responding to Kota Baru Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan's call for the government to
explain the constitutional basis
for the removal of the exco members.
During his debate on the 2027 Supply Bill in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, Takiyuddin said the move conflicted with the Negri Sembilan Constitution and questioned the Attorney-General's position that the revocation was valid.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said last month that the revocation of the 10 exco members'
appointments was valid
under the state constitution.
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had earlier said that any termination of exco members without his advice
had no legal effect
.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Muhyiddin: PN deregistration reminder to treat component parties fairly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin described the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional's registration as a reminder for coalition leaders to treat all component parties fairly.
The Bersatu president said coalition leadership must also comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966.
"Do not abuse power or position for the interests of a particular party or group to the extent that the coalition deviates from its original purpose and objectives," he said in a statement today.
Muhyiddin, who is also PN's founder, said he was saddened by the decision to cancel the coalition's registration.
"I will discuss the way forward with Bersatu leaders at a special Political Bureau meeting tonight," said the Pagoh MP.
Earlier today, the Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) confirmed it cancelled PN's registration, saying the coalition's explanation failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after
reviewing the documents
and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: All 242 Mara-sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid ongoing unrest.
Mara deputy director-general (education) Zahari Aziz said all 242 students were safe based on the latest reports from student representatives at their universities, with none reported involved in the unrest.
"Academic activities are continuing as usual. In areas experiencing public transport disruptions, the universities have taken appropriate measures to conduct classes online," he said in a statement today.
He said Mara, through its overseas office in Frankfurt, Germany, remained in close contact with the students and reminded them to stay alert and avoid demonstration areas.
The students were advised to follow instructions issued by local authorities and the Malaysian Embassy in Paris, he said.
"Mara will continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority," he said. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Timeline: Perikatan Nasional's rise and fall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional (PN) was formed on Aug 7, 2020, following an idea mooted by its then president, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin.
It currently comprises four component parties: Pas, Bersatu, Parti Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Gerakan) and Parti Rakyat India Malaysia (MIPP).
The collapse of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) government led by Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad following the "Sheraton Move" in February 2020 paved the way for the formation of the PN government.
At the time, PN comprised Bersatu, Pas, Gerakan, Sabah Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) and the Sabah Progressive Party (SAPP). The coalition sought to champion the people's interests regardless of race, religion or region, and to govern the country with integrity.
Tensions within PN have escalated, with several senior Bersatu leaders resigning, including Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, who announced his resignation as PN secretary-general and Selangor PN chairman.
PN's current official membership comprises Pas, Gerakan, MIPP, Parti Pejuang Tanah Air (Pejuang) and Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan).
On Sept 23, the Registrar of Societies (RoS)
suspended all PN activities.
Today, RoS cancelled PN's registration.
Perikatan Nasional: Key dates
Feb 23, 2020 – The Sheraton Move triggered a political crisis that led to the end of the Pakatan Harapan (PH) government.
Feb 24, 2020 – Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad resigned as prime minister.
Feb 29, 2020 – The Yang di-Pertuan Agong appointed Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin as the eighth prime minister.
March 1, 2020 – Muhyiddin was sworn in as prime minister.
March 9, 2020 – The new Cabinet was announced.
May 17, 2020 – A memorandum of understanding on political cooperation was signed by parties supporting the government at the time.
Aug 7, 2020 – PN was officially registered with the Registrar of Societies (RoS).
Aug 19, 2020 – Parti Progresif Sabah (SAPP) and Pas officially joined PN.
Feb 11, 2021 – Gerakan joined PN.
Aug 16, 2021 – Muhyiddin resigned as prime minister after losing majority support.
Nov 19, 2022 – PN won 74 parliamentary seats in the 15th General Election.
Dec 5, 2022 – Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) left PN.
January 2023 – Gerakan denied leaving PN.
April 22, 2024 – Parti Rakyat India Malaysia (MIPP) joined PN.
Dec 14, 2024 – SAPP left PN, ending its membership in the coalition.
Dec 30, 2025 – Muhyiddin announced his resignation as PN chairman, effective Jan 1, 2026.
Feb 22, 2026 – Pas vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar was appointed PN chairman.
June 22, 2026 – Pejuang joined PN.
July 6, 2026 – Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) joined PN.
Sept 23, 2026 – RoS suspended all PN activities.
Oct 5, 2026 – PN filed an application for judicial review at the High Court to challenge the suspension notice issued by RoS.
Oct 20, 2026 – RoS cancelled PN's registration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SME Bank to channel RM2.8bil under 2027 Budget to boost businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SME Bank will channel about RM2.8 billion under the 2027 Budget to strengthen the competitiveness of Malaysian businesses across seven priority sectors.
The initiatives form part of more than RM7 billion in government-mandated programmes allocated through SME Bank's parent Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd.
SME Bank chief executive officer Samad Majid Zain said the initiatives will help businesses adopt technology, improve productivity, operate sustainably and expand into new markets.
He said the bank will leverage Bank Pembangunan's capabilities to support enterprise development, aligning with the government's economic reform agenda and the 13th Malaysia Plan.
Of the allocation, RM558 million will support entrepreneurship development through financing and grants for Bumiputera entrepreneurs, women-owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), franchise and licensing businesses, and underserved groups.
Another RM500 million will support tourism businesses, comprising RM200 million under the Special Fund for Tourism and RM300 million under the Tourism Programme.
Dana Kelestarian Alam 2.0 will receive RM600 million to finance companies undertaking low-carbon initiatives and investing in sustainable business operations.
Meanwhile, RM500 million will be channelled through the Technology Adoption Fund to support technology adoption, digitalisation and Industry 4.0 initiatives, including industrialised building system component contractors, manufacturers and installers.
A further RM400 million will support transportation, logistics, maritime, oil and gas, and aerospace businesses including maintenance, repair and overhaul activities.
The Local Acceleration and Growth Programme will receive RM200 million to provide affordable financing for manufacturers, service providers and local vendors to improve capacity, productivity and competitiveness.
The fund is also to strengthen their participation in the supply chains of multinational corporations and major Malaysian companies.
Separately, a RM3 million grant under the Business Export Programme will help Bumiputera MSMEs in the services and manufacturing sectors strengthen their export readiness and access overseas markets.
Samad said SME Bank would prioritise measurable development outcomes, additionality and effective programme delivery, in line with Bank Negara Malaysia's Performance Measurement Framework.
He said the initiatives were aimed at helping businesses become more competitive, create jobs and contribute to stronger communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia takes lead role in Asean anti-money laundering efforts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strengthened its role in combating transnational crime after being selected as the Voluntary Lead Shepherd of the ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) Working Group on Money Laundering.
The Home Ministry said that the appointment was agreed upon at the Preparatory SOMTC for the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC) and Related Meetings in Makati, the Philippines.
The Malaysian delegation to the preparatory meeting was led by ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman.
"The meeting aimed to coordinate positions and finalise substantive preparations for the ministerial meetings scheduled for Oct 20 and 21.
"It also adopted the Terms of Reference for the SOMTC Working Group on Money Laundering, with Malaysia serving as the Voluntary Lead Shepherd for this priority area," the ministry said in a statement.
Awang Alik also co-chaired the Preparatory SOMTC for the 13th AMMTC Plus China Consultation, aimed at strengthening Asean-China cooperation in addressing transnational crime threats.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail will lead the Malaysian delegation to the two-day 20th AMMTC, which begins today.
The ministry said the meeting, chaired by the Philippines, brings together Asean ministers responsible for security and transnational crime to strengthen regional cooperation against increasingly complex criminal threats.
Besides attending the 20th AMMTC, Saifuddin Nasution is scheduled to participate in four consultations with Asean dialogue partners - the 16th AMMTC Plus Three, 13th AMMTC Plus China, 11th AMMTC Plus Japan and 7th AMMTC Plus Korea.
The ministry said strategic cooperation with China, Japan and South Korea was crucial to strengthening the preparedness of regional enforcement agencies amid an evolving transnational crime landscape.
Malaysia will also co-chair the 13th AMMTC Plus China Consultation, in line with its role as Asean Country Coordinator for Asean-China cooperation in combating transnational crime.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France vows fresh curfews as PM scrambles to restore order after riots
Article:
PARIS: France will impose new curfews where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, as authorities sought to restore order after weekend demonstrations degenerated into riots.
The eurozone's second-largest economy was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst street violence in recent years, just six months before the country elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
Images of clashes and public buildings set on fire or vandalised circulated around the world, prompting several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.
Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday.
The targeted measures had "helped keep the night calm," Lecornu said.
Macron, currently on a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, has acknowledged shortcomings in the handling of the protests.
The presidency said Macron had secured the delivery of an additional 200,000 tonnes of diesel per month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain during the tour.
- TARGETED CURFEWS-
Lecornu said that new curfews would be decided "where the situation requires it."
"Targeted curfews have contributed to calm overnight," he wrote on X.
The government scheduled another series of emergency meetings on Tuesday, including talks involving representatives of major social media platforms.
Under pressure, Lecornu will convene political parties for a meeting on Thursday, a member of his team said. He will also meet with trade unions on Wednesday.
The government has come under criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a "wake-up call" that exposed a "profound crisis" of authority.
Police confirmed the night had passed without major incidents across France.
Several cities, including Paris, the southwestern city of Bordeaux and Nice on the French Riviera, introduced partial curfews on Monday in response to urban unrest that followed weeks of student demonstrations over poor learning conditions in high schools.
While some restrictions, such as those in Paris, initially applied only for the night from Monday to Tuesday, others, particularly in Bordeaux and Nice, were set to remain in force for several days.
During the night, a helicopter flew over the French capital's Place de la Republique, one of the epicentres of the unrest, sweeping a powerful searchlight across the square to monitor compliance with the curfew.
In Lyon, despite a ban on demonstrations, around 500 people gathered on Monday evening outside the tourism office that was set on fire, to show support for shopkeepers affected by looting, according to organisers.
The word "LYON" had been spelled out on the ground with candles.
A banner hung on a fence nearby read "Anti-Rioters Lyon" and "Doucet Resign", referring to Green mayor Gregory Doucet, an AFP journalist said.
- 'CLOSE UP YOUR BORDERS' -
Nationwide, more than 2,500 people have been taken into police custody since the weekend, and 67 people had been jailed.
Some demonstrators were seriously injured. In the eastern city of Mulhouse, a 17-year-old girl lost an eye. In Saint-Etienne, a 17-year-old boy had his hand blown off by a grenade.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday, saying police "had lost control" during the unrest. Macron rejected his resignation.
Finance Minister Roland Lescure has pledged support measures for shopkeepers and craftspeople.
Patrick Martin, the head of France's Medef business lobby group, on Tuesday accused the state of having "failed" during the urban unrest that hit at least 3,000 businesses, according to preliminary estimates.
Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, as the upcoming midterm elections force his Republican party to face strong headwinds.
"What's happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything," Trump told reporters in Washington.
"It's immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: On Israeli election eve, settler violence becomes Netanyahu liability
Article:
ATTACKS on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank have turned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's championing of settlers into a potential liability days before elections, with opponents calling him soft on "Jewish terrorism."
Leading opposition contenders Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Golan and Naftali Bennett, whose politics range widely, all referred to the attacks as "Jewish terrorism" – a term of the sort that the Netanyahu government bristles at when levelled from abroad.
In separate incidents, settlers ambushed both US photographer Heidi Levine, who remains in hospital, and a European delegation including the top French official in Jerusalem when they went to Palestinian villages east of Ramallah for the olive harvest.
Several Palestinians have been killed in the near-daily attacks by settlers during the harvest which have included beatings, arson and theft.
"What is happening in the West Bank is Jewish terrorism under the auspices of the Israeli government," said centre-right candidate Eisenkot, a former military chief and Netanyahu's main rival in the Oct 27 vote.
Similarly, Yair Golan, from the centre-left, said that "Jewish terror must be fought with an iron fist, just as Palestinian terror is fought," and vowed to restore order in the West Bank should he come to power.
Golan went to visit Levine in hospital, while President Isaac Herzog, who holds a largely ceremonial role, spoke to her by phone.
Netanyahu has challenged the accounts of the attacks and pointed out that Bernard Baudoux, a 78-year-old French mayor who was beaten up, is a leftist supporter of the Palestinian cause.
"These reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest," Netanyahu's office said in a statement, referring to the West Bank by its Biblical name.
Boaz Bismuth, a member of parliament for Netanyahu's Likud party, said in a television interview that "there is no Jewish terrorism in Judea and Samaria."
Netanyahu, in a UN address last month delivered amid mounting international criticism, said the violence was the work of a small number of juvenile delinquents.
Polls show that a dwindling number of Israelis support a Palestinian state, especially after the unprecedented Oct 7, 2023 attack by Hamas from Gaza.
But experts say settler violence, long off the radar politically in Israel, is another matter.
[[nid:1559810]]
"Even though Israeli society leans to the right and people aren't supportive of a territorial solution right now (with Palestinians), there is high consensus against settler violence," said Alon Yakter, a political scientist at Tel Aviv University.
"This became a soft belly for Netanyahu because he's allied with parties that want to divert the conversation (on settler violence) or treat them as a few rotten apples," said Yakter, who specialises in voting patterns.
He said that the settler violence itself is unlikely to determine how Israelis vote, but it could feed into two issues that matter most to Israeli voters – security and governance.
"It's better for them (opposition leaders) to portray this violence as a lack of control and governance hurting our security interests," he said.
Eisenkot has vowed to restore the use of administrative detention, through which Israel can detain a suspect without charge, for Jewish suspects.
Under Netanyahu, whose government includes far-right advocates of annexing the West Bank, administrative detention applies only to Palestinians.
Eisenkot vowed to use "an iron fist" against anyone acting outside the law and to prevent settler raids and arson against Palestinians.
Netanyahu's government, one of the most right-wing in Israel's history, has approved or legalised 104 settlements since coming to power in 2022.
More than 500,000 Israeli settlers live across the West Bank, in settlements that are illegal under international law.
Mairav Zonszein, senior analyst on Israel for the International Crisis Group, said that while the settler attacks would not alter the vote, they had made Netanyahu's response an election issue.
"It's part of a discourse about how Netanyahu is actually hurting Israeli national security," she said.
"Netanyahu's statements make him look so beholden to the settler movement and it looks ridiculous just to kind of pretend like (these attacks) didn't actually happen."
But she doubted whether a different future prime minister would ultimately question settlements themselves.
Opposition leaders are "going after the most egregious elements of settler violence but they are not going to upend the settlement enterprise," she said.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court sets Jan 20 for ex-TH senior manager's bribery appeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has fixed Jan 20 next year to hear the appeal by a former senior manager of Lembaga Tabung Haji against his conviction and sentence of three years' jail and an RM852,385 fine for accepting RM170,477 in bribes.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin set the date during case management involving Zaharuddin Hamid, 53, a former senior manager (technical) of the Real Estate Development Section.
"The parties must file their written submissions on or before Jan 8 next year," she said.
Zaharuddin, who was present at today's proceedings, filed the appeal in November 2023.
According to the three charges, Zaharuddin is accused of corruptly accepting bribes totalling RM170,477 from Yusaidi Mohd through Amaneez Creative Solution, via cheques deposited into a Maybank account belonging to his sister, Zanita Hamid.
The payments were allegedly inducements to recommend Consoline Sdn Bhd and MNB Engineering Sdn Bhd for office renovation works at TH Ipoh (IFiC), Perak, as well as TH Muar, TH Batu Pahat and TH Kluang in Johor.
He is accused of committing the three offences at Maybank Desa Pandan here between Oct 5, 2015 and May 24, 2018.
The charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009, which provides for a maximum of 20 years' imprisonment and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Earlier, Zaharuddin's counsel, A. Ashok, informed the court that the defence received the appeal record this morning and applied for a hearing date. Deputy public prosecutor Haresh Prakash Somiah confirmed the matter.
The trial began in 2022, with the prosecution calling 18 witnesses and the defence calling only the accused.
On Nov 30, 2023, Sessions Court judge Rozina Ayob sentenced Zaharuddin to three years' imprisonment and an RM852,385 fine after finding him guilty on all three charges.
The court also ordered that he serve 15 months' imprisonment if he fails to settle the fine.
However, the court granted Zaharuddin a stay of execution pending the outcome of his appeal. —BERNAMA

Title: Imported vegetable glut hurting local growers, says Mohamad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security is working with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) to tackle the oversupply of imported vegetables, which is hurting local producers.
Its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the discussions also took into account the implementation of the requirement to submit a Certificate of Analysis (CoA), which became mandatory on June 1, 2026, although some views held that the measure was still insufficient.
"We have brought this matter up for discussion at the food security level, and we are analysing what new measures need to be introduced to protect the position of vegetable growers in Malaysia, as well as those involved in fruit production," he said during the question-and-answer session in Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards.
Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (Maqis).
He said commodities facing oversupply included chillies, cabbage, round cabbage, mustard greens, tomatoes and cucumbers, prompting complaints from local growers, including those in Cameron Highlands and Johor.
In response to Wong's original question on the performance of myGAP certification since the introduction of e-myGAP in 2020, Mohamad said the system was introduced to shorten the certification period from two years to 90 working days without compromising compliance with Malaysian Standards (MS).
However, he said the timeframe depended on the farm's level of readiness and the applicant's compliance with all stipulated certification requirements.
Based on records, Mohamad said the number of applications increased from 2,507 in 2021 to 3,652 in 2025, while 3,282 applications were recorded for 2026 as of the reporting cut-off.
Of these, the number of applications successfully certified in less than 90 working days stood at 324 in 2021, 163 in 2022, 183 in 2023, 373 in 2024, 249 in 2025 and 206 in 2026.
However, he said most applications still took more than 90 working days to process, involving 2,097 applications in 2021, 1,895 in 2022, 3,277 in 2023, 2,967 in 2024 and 3,106 in 2025. This was partly due to the need to carry out corrective actions to address identified non-compliance.
Meanwhile, responding to a supplementary question from Nurul Amin Hamid (PN-Padang Terap) on market preference for myGAP-certified produce and guidance for smallholders, Mohamad said the Department of Agriculture would assist farm operators in obtaining certification once applications had been submitted.
He said the ministry had also asked the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) to intervene in marketing agricultural produce when oversupply caused selling prices to fall below production costs.
"This happens when, for example, the selling prices of chillies, okra or other crops fall too low, below production costs. We then ask Fama to intervene so that farmers and small-scale vegetable growers do not incur losses when there is an oversupply in the market," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ahmad Samsuri questions timing of PN deregistration
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Perikatan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has questioned the timing of the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), describing the move as unusual.
In a statement posted on his Facebook page, Samsuri said the decision, made just two days before the case was due to be heard in court and ahead of the Melaka election candidate nominations, raised questions about its motive.
"What happened before the case was brought to court was an unusual action. Indeed, it was extraordinary, and could even be considered abnormal.
"All actions that coincided with the timeline leading up to the Melaka election candidate nominations, when the Election Commission (EC) had only two days earlier written to 'PN' seeking a response on the use of the 'PN' logo, clearly show a fear of this coalition," he said.
He warned that the move would not diminish public support for PN.
"Remember, the people's wave will not easily be extinguished by politicians hiding behind their power.
"Especially politicians who make 'working towards banning this coalition' a key performance indicator (KPI) to align themselves with those we face in the election," he said.
Earlier, RoS confirmed the cancellation of PN's registration after finding that the coalition's explanations and representations submitted on Oct 12 failed to rebut the grounds stated in its earlier notice.
RoS said the decision was made under Subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), after reviewing all documents and representations submitted by PN.
Before that, RoS issued a notice dated Sept 22 under Subsection 13(2) of the same Act, allowing PN to explain why its registration should not be cancelled.
RoS said the explanation provided did not offer sufficient justification to maintain PN's registration, while stressing that all registered organisations are responsible for complying with the law and their respective constitutions.

Title: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia fails to strike out SUV defect lawsuits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mercedes-Benz Malaysia Sdn Bhd has failed in its bid to have lawsuits over alleged defects in its GLE 450 4M AMG luxury sports utility vehicle (SUV) dismissed.
High Court judicial commissioner Datin Zalita Zaidan upheld the lower court's decision to dismiss the company's application to strike out lawsuits brought by Beyond Natural Group Sdn Bhd and two individuals, S. Aruna and G. Hanulraj.
The lawsuits concern alleged mechanical and electronic defects in the SUV, including battery failure, airbag warning malfunctions and a fire underneath a car seat.
The court was told that the vehicle was ordered from authorised Mercedes-Benz dealer Hap Seng Star Sdn Bhd on June 25, 2022.
It was registered under Beyond Natural Group and financed through a hire-purchase agreement dated Oct 21.
The vehicle was primarily driven by Aruna and occasionally used by Hanulraj for daily and business travel.
The plaintiffs claimed that the SUV began experiencing serious mechanical and electronic problems during the manufacturer's warranty period.
On Dec 8, a warning stating "the front-passenger airbag disabled" appeared on the vehicle's instrument panel, raising concerns over passenger safety.
On Dec 23, another warning stating "48V Battery See Owner's Manual" appeared, leaving the vehicle unable to start.
The plaintiffs filed lawsuits seeking damages for alleged breaches of statutory guarantees under the Consumer Protection Act and Sale of Goods Act, breach of warranty, misrepresentation and negligence.
Aruna and Hanulraj also sought damages for pain, suffering, stress and trauma allegedly caused by the incidents.
Mercedes-Benz Malaysia, the wholesale distributor of Mercedes-Benz vehicles in the country, applied to strike out the claims on the grounds that the plaintiffs lacked legal standing to sue.
The company argued that the bank was the vehicle's legal owner under the hire-purchase agreement, while Beyond Natural Group was merely the hirer.
It also argued that Aruna and Hanulraj were not parties to the purchase agreement and had no contractual or ownership rights over the vehicle.
In her grounds of judgment dated Oct 19, Zalita said the allegations raised issues that required a full trial, including expert testimony and cross-examination.
"The question of whether recurring 48V battery shutdowns and airbag instrument warnings not forgetting the fire which occurred underneath the car seat, constitute inherent latent defects issue, breach of implied conditions, or negligence that require expert witness testimony and cross-examination at trial," she said.
Zalita rejected the company's arguments, saying the hire-purchase arrangement did not automatically deprive the plaintiffs of their right to pursue legal action.
"The 1st Defendant's contention that hire-purchase financing completely extinguishes locus standi is legally flawed," she said.
The court said actual users and beneficial purchasers who relied on representations or warranties concerning a vehicle's quality retained statutory rights to claim damages.
Zalita said striking out the claims at this stage could create an unacceptable situation in which only financial institutions, despite having no knowledge of a vehicle's technical problems, would have the legal standing to sue.
"Striking out their claims at an interlocutory stage would create an unacceptable absurdity in consumer law where financial institutions, who possess zero knowledge of vehicle technical defects would be the sole entities with standing, thereby insulating manufacturers and wholesale distributors from product liability."
Zalita said Mercedes-Benz Malaysia had failed to establish grounds for striking out the claims.
The court also ordered the company to pay RM14,000 in costs to the three plaintiffs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Father devastated after daughter dies following breathing emergency
Article:
SEPANG: A father was left heartbroken after his daughter, whom he had sent to school as usual yesterday, died after reportedly suffering breathing difficulties caused by an obstructed airway.
Mior Shahrizal Mior Zakaria, 48, said he rushed to Sekolah Kebangsaan Dengkil after being informed that his youngest child, Derma Damiya Nur Mikayla, was having breathing difficulties.
He said the Year One pupil was found unconscious on the second-floor corridor when he arrived.
"I tried to help her, including performing resuscitation, but she did not respond.
"About 15 minutes later, the ambulance arrived, but my daughter was still completely unresponsive," he said when met at the Pekan Dengkil Muslim Cemetery here today.
Mior Shahrizal said doctors told him the girl's airway was believed to have been blocked by food, possibly a banana or a piece of chicken, although the exact cause had yet to be established.
Recalling their time together, he said he had quit his job in early January to focus on his daughter's schooling, including sending her to and picking her up from school every day.
She attended religious school in the morning before continuing her lessons at the national school in the afternoon.
He also noticed a change in her behaviour a day before the incident, saying she appeared more independent than usual.
"Normally, she would be reluctant to shower when she returned from religious school. But yesterday, when I asked her to shower, she got up and did it herself.
"She also put on her school uniform and tudung without asking for my help, as she usually did," he said.
He described his daughter as active and close to him, adding that she often shared stories and confided in him whenever she faced problems.
Despite his grief, Mior Shahrizal said he accepted the loss as God's will.
The girl's body was collected from the Putrajaya Hospital Forensic Unit at about noon before being taken to Masjid Jamiatus Solehah in Pekan Dengkil for funeral prayers.
She was later laid to rest at the Pekan Dengkil Muslim Cemetery, where about 50 family members and relatives, including her mother, Derma Taksiah, 51, attended the burial.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-Switzerland trade hits RM13.4bil, up 9.8pct in 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Switzerland bilateral trade reached RM13.4 billion in 2025, an increase of 9.8 per cent from the previous year, reflecting continued growth in economic ties between the two countries.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said that as of June, 211 manufacturing projects involving Swiss participation had been implemented in Malaysia, attracting RM12.8 billion in investments and creating 19,744 jobs.
He welcomed more quality investments that could strengthen local industries and create high-skilled job opportunities for Malaysians.
"We also discussed the Malaysia-Efta Economic Partnership Agreement (Meepa) and efforts to strengthen investment cooperation.
"I emphasised the importance of implementing Meepa to expand market access and create more opportunities for businesses in both countries, while reaffirming Malaysia's commitment to sustainable industrial development and trade," he said in a Facebook post today.
Johari also shared photographs of his meeting with Swiss State Secretary for Economic Affairs Helene Budliger Artieda, who paid him a courtesy call at his office here.
He said the meeting provided an opportunity to strengthen trade and investment cooperation, particularly in advanced manufacturing, precision engineering and medical technology.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia agree to expand online safety cooperation
Article:
BALI: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address online child safety issues, with efforts also planned to involve Singapore in the collaboration.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said online safety, particularly involving children, was an important issue requiring the collective attention of countries in the region.
"We are working towards holding a trilateral meeting involving Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore, InsyaAllah, in December, if schedules permit," he told Bernama after a bilateral meeting with his Indonesian counterpart, Meutya Hafid, on Tuesday.
He said that although Asean countries have different laws and implementation approaches, the initiative by Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore could encourage other countries in the region to participate.
"We not only have aligned policies, but may also have several similar mechanisms, although they may not be exactly the same."
Fahmi also welcomed Meutya's intention to strengthen cooperation between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Indonesia's Communication and Digital Affairs Ministry.
MCMC's experience in handling public complaints related to social media could also be useful to the Indonesian authorities, he added.
In a related development, Singapore's Digital Development and Information Minister Josephine Teo said she and Fahmi had exchanged views on developments in their respective telecommunications sectors during an impromptu meeting at Ngurah Rai International Airport on Monday.
In a post on her official social media account, Teo said the discussions included quantum-safe communications, as well as online safety for children and young people.
She also expressed hope of hosting Fahmi in Singapore in the near future.
Teo happened to meet Fahmi, who had just arrived in Bali, while she was waiting for her flight back to Singapore after attending Bali Tech Week 2026.
Fahmi is in Bali at the invitation of the organisers to deliver a keynote address at Bali Tech Week.
He was accompanied by MCMC Deputy Managing Director (Regulatory) Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibudden and First Secretary (Economics) at the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta, Fakhrul Arifin Mohammad Zulkifly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN yet to decide logo for Melaka polls after deregistration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has yet to decide which logo its candidates will use in the upcoming Melaka election following the coalition's deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS) today.
PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said it was too early to make a decision, adding that candidates could still contest under a component party's logo even without a registered coalition brand.
"PN comprises Pas, Wawasan, Gerakan, Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP) and Pejuang. We can discuss which logo to use, just as Pakatan Harapan used the PKR logo in the 2018 general election.
"At the time, it worked out fine. DAP, Bersatu and Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu did not object," he said at a press conference in Parliament today.
Takiyuddin said there was still time to decide before the Melaka election on Oct 31.
Earlier, the RoS announced that it had cancelled PN's registration after finding that the coalition's explanations failed to address the grounds stated in an earlier notice.
The decision was made under Subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of Act 832 after the RoS reviewed documents and representations submitted by PN on Oct 12.
Takiyuddin also denied allegations that Pas, himself and PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar were responsible for the deregistration.
He said PN had already submitted details to the RoS explaining why Bersatu was not invited to the coalition's Supreme Leadership Council meeting on July 16, a decision cited as grounds for the cancellation.
He said PN's practice was to exclude any component party facing internal disputes, including contested leadership positions, from coalition meetings to avoid questions over the validity of decisions made.
Takiyuddin cited MIPP's internal leadership dispute in January, saying he had written to the party to suspend its participation in PN meetings until the matter was resolved.
He said a similar approach was taken with Bersatu after four of its MPs — Sabak Bernam, Sungai Besar, Kangar and Kulim-Bandar Baru — lodged a complaint with the RoS on July 13 over the quorum of a Bersatu Supreme Leadership Council meeting.
The following day, Takiyuddin said he wrote to Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, raising PN's concerns and asking the party to clarify the situation or seek clarification from the RoS.
He said Bersatu was informed that it would not be invited to PN meetings until the matter was resolved.
Takiyuddin added that PN also considered Bersatu's decision to use its own logo in the Negri Sembilan state election, announced by Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin on July 15.
He said Bersatu's decision indicated that it did not wish to use the PN logo, which was another reason it was not invited to the July 16 meeting to decide on the coalition's logo and candidates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
Article:
BEIJING: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move "overstretched" the concept of national security.
China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months.
The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China.
Beijing's foreign ministry opposed the ban on Tuesday, vowing to protect Chinese businesses.
"China has consistently opposed the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicisation of issues related to science, technology, and trade," ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference.
The Department of Homeland Security can issue directions to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services.
Its statement on Monday said that "DeepSeek's models multiple threat vectors" and must be removed from IT devices.
Use of DeepSeek AI tools "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors," the department warned.
Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government "extensive authority" to access private company infrastructure, it said.
AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment.
DeepSeek, one of China's top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance.
The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4.
The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals.
Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a "communication channel" for AI incidents.
The topic is expected to arise again when the countries' leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Spanish landlords feel attacked as housing crisis overshadows vote
Article:
MADRID: Landlady Maria Jose Fernandez feels unfairly portrayed as a property speculator amid the tensions over Spain's housing crisis, just weeks before a snap nationwide election.
The housing debate intensified after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted in September from her lifelong home and died a few days later, sparking nationwide protests.
Fernandez, a 65-year-old retiree, said the problems faced by property owners like her were being overlooked and feared government proposals to strengthen tenants' rights would make matters worse.
A couple renting her roughly 50-square-metre (540-square-foot) apartment in Cercedilla, a mountain town near Madrid, stopped paying the monthly rent of 710 euros (US$800) in 2024.
"It took me nearly two years to get an eviction date," she told AFP, describing the experience as devastating both emotionally and financially.
Unable to keep paying the rent on her own home, she was forced to move in with her daughter.
Housing is set to feature in Spain's November 29 snap election, with landlords concerned about tighter regulations and housing activists demanding greater protection for tenants.
Much of the public anger has been directed at "vulture funds" – firms accused of buying up homes and then hiking the rents to maximise profits.
Hundreds of tents have occupied Madrid's central Puerta del Sol square since the property company that owns Abascal's flat drastically raised her rent and the old lady was evicted on a stretcher.
- Plans on hold -
In response to the protests, Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's minority government tried – but failed – to pass new housing measures.
These included a ban on evicting vulnerable tenants through 2030 and the introduction of indefinite rental contracts.
The proposals were voted down and Sanchez called an early election.
In 2023, his government introduced a housing law that strengthened tenants' rights, as well as giving regional and local authorities new tools to curb rents.
But some measures – including rent controls in areas officially designated as facing high housing demand – met resistance in regions governed by the conservative opposition Popular Party (PP).
Meanwhile, rents and property prices continued to climb as demand outstripped supply.
Average rents have almost doubled in Spain over the past decade, according to real estate website Idealista.
Javier Medina, who owned 11 rental properties generating around 10,000 euros a month, predicted indefinite rent contracts "would be the end of my business."
The government "doesn't help me and on top of that it wants to penalise me!" the 32-year-old told AFP.
Medina, who rents a home with his wife and two children, said he understood Spain faced a serious housing affordability problem.
But he wants "clear rules of the game that don't keep changing" and has put plans to develop his property business on hold until after the election.
- 'Leave us alone' -
Medina said the public debate had made it difficult to admit to being a property investor, which was "viewed very badly."
Protesters have chanted slogans including "Landlords are thieves" and "Landlords steal our wages" at demonstrations in Madrid.
Socialist spokeswoman Montse Minguez criticised vulture funds during parliamentary debates.
But she resigned last week after it emerged that her partner's company owned around 30 rental properties.
Maria, a 38-year-old landlord in Catalonia who declined to give her surname for fear of being identified by her tenants, said she too felt unfairly targeted.
"Now we're all supposedly murderers because Maricarmen died," she told AFP, saying it made her "very angry."
"Leave us alone!".
Maria, who had built up a portfolio of 30 properties over two decades, rejected being lumped together with large investment funds the government wants to prevent from buying up homes on a large scale.
"I'm not a vulture fund!" she said.
The prospect of tighter restrictions has made her consider leaving the rental market altogether.
"As my apartments become vacant, I'll sell them," she said.
The Federation of Real Estate Associations has forecast that rental transactions could fall by up to 30 per cent in the coming weeks, potentially reducing supply further and pushing prices higher.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Policeman hurt in Tanah Merah parang attack discharged
Article:
TANAH MERAH: A policeman who was injured in a parang attack during an anti-drug raid here on Saturday has been discharged from Tanah Merah Hospital after his condition improved.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the 37-year-old corporal was in stable condition and had been allowed to return home.
He said investigations into the suspect were still ongoing.
"The suspect, in his 30s, is believed to have been involved in several other cases, including drug-related offences.
"We have yet to determine when the suspect will be charged, as investigations are still ongoing," he said.
On Saturday, a police corporal was seriously injured after being
slashed
with a parang by a suspected drug pusher during an anti-drug operation in Kampung Lalalang Pepuyu.
The policeman suffered a fractured left hand in the 1.35pm incident.

Title: LBS rewards homebuyers with prizes in 65th-anniversary campaign
Article:
KULA LUMPUR: For 150 homebuyers of LBS Bina Group Bhd, the joy of owning a home came with an added reason to celebrate, as the property developer rewarded them with an array of prizes under its 65th-anniversary campaign.
LBS marked the conclusion of its "Celebrate 65. Score More Than a Home" campaign with a special prize presentation ceremony, extending its anniversary celebrations to the homeowners who have been part of the group's journey.
The 150 winners received a range of prizes, including a five-day, four-night trip to England for two, eight signed football jerseys, 11 gold bars and 30 Traveloka vouchers.
LBS executive director Datuk Cynthia Lim presented the prizes to the winning homebuyers at the ceremony, recognising their support and expressing the group's appreciation for the trust they have placed in the developer.
LBS group executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Lim Hock San said the group's 65th anniversary was not only a milestone in its corporate journey but also an opportunity to celebrate the homeowners who had contributed to its growth.
"Reaching our 65th anniversary is a proud milestone for LBS, but what truly makes this journey special is the trust our homeowners have placed in us. Every home represents a dream, a new beginning and a future built with their loved ones. For us, handing over the keys is never the end of the story; it is the beginning of a lasting relationship.
"Through our 'Score More Than a Home' campaign, we wanted to celebrate our homeowners and show our appreciation for being part of the LBS journey. My heartiest congratulations to all 150 winners. We hope these rewards bring smiles, create wonderful memories and add a little more excitement to your homeownership journey as we celebrate this milestone together," Lim said in a statement.
The campaign featured selected developments across LBS' property portfolio, including SkyRia, Astella, Aulica, KITA Sejati, KITA Avenue, Prestige and Centrum Iris.
By bringing its anniversary celebrations directly to homebuyers, LBS aims to make the homeownership experience more rewarding while strengthening relationships with its customers beyond the purchase of a property.
As it builds on its 65-year legacy in the property development industry, the group said it remained focused on creating more than homes by delivering meaningful homeownership experiences and fostering lasting connections with the people and communities it serves.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina: Teachers handling bullying cases need trauma support, counselling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Teachers handling bullying and violence cases in schools should receive trauma management training, confidential counselling and psychological support to help them cope with the emotional toll.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said also proposed incorporating Trauma-Informed Teaching into teacher training to help educators recognise and respond appropriately to students experiencing trauma.
"We often ask how teachers can protect students.
"But we seldom ask: who protects teachers when they themselves have to face trauma and violence in schools?
"Teachers are also human beings with feelings. Teachers too can experience fear, stress and trauma," she said at the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 Literacy Programme at the Malaysian Teacher Education Institute's Malay Language Campus today.
Azalina said teachers could be traumatised by witnessing students being beaten, listening to disclosures from children who had experienced sexual harassment or facing angry parents following bullying incidents.
"We cannot expect teachers to always be strong to protect others while their own emotional wellbeing is not given attention.
"Therefore, teachers who look after the emotions of students also deserve protection of their own emotions," she said.
She cited Singapore, where education staff have access to counselling and wellbeing support, and New Zealand, where trauma intervention teams help schools manage incidents that could affect the wellbeing of students and staff.
In England, Azalina said, the Education Staff Wellbeing Charter addressed staff wellbeing.
"I am of the view that it is time we look into a more comprehensive approach in providing emotional support to teachers who handle bullying and violence cases in schools," she said.
She said Trauma-Informed Teaching was not intended to turn teachers into psychologists, but to equip them with the skills to recognise signs of trauma, respond safely and identify when professional help was needed.
"Teachers should not be left alone when facing the trauma of their students," she added.
Azalina also called for an end to the perception that bullying was simply part of growing up.
"Bullying is not a joke, bullying is also not training to make someone stronger and bullying is not a form of discipline," she said.
She said legislation alone could not eradicate bullying, adding that teachers were often among the first to recognise when a student was suffering.
"The law can only provide protection, but teachers in schools are among the first individuals who can detect a student's suffering," she added.
Azalina urged trainee teachers to reach out to students who suddenly became withdrawn, were afraid to attend school or distanced themselves from friends, rather than dismissing such changes as normal.
The Anti-Bullying Act 2026 came into force with the launch of the
Anti-Bullying Tribunal
on June 16.
Azalina told the Dewan Rakyat in December last year that primary and secondary schools had reported an average of more than
14,000 bullying cases
annually since 2019.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-MP says army plan for migrant deportations is 'playing to the gallery'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Klang member of parliament Charles Santiago said Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin was playing to the gallery over his proposal to deploy soldiers to help deport undocumented migrants.
During the 2027 Budget debate on Monday, Radzi proposed mobilising soldiers to assist the Immigration Department in a nationwide crackdown on undocumented migrants.
Santiago said Malaysia should first examine how the system produced irregular migration before deploying the army.
He cited the 2026 United States Trafficking in Persons Report, which he said flagged that not a single employment agency in Malaysia had been prosecuted under the Private Employment Agencies Act between 2025 and 2026.
"More troublingly, it identifies official complicity as a significant concern," he said in a statement on X.
Santiago added that Radzi had himself acknowledged that civil servants assist traffickers.
"So why are we proposing to send soldiers after the workers? Why aren't we going after those who profit from and sustain this system?" he asked.
Santiago said that if the army were deployed, it should target other groups.
"Deploy the army? Then deploy it against the employers, that knowingly hire undocumented workers," he said.
"Deploy it against recruitment cartels that manufacture debt bondage, and against corrupt officials who enable labour trafficking."
Santiago said Malaysia had repeatedly faced international scrutiny and embarrassment over its poor labour migration governance.
"We simply cannot deport our way out of a system that we have failed to govern. So stop scapegoating migrant workers and start holding the powerful accountable."
He highlighted that, while the law caps placement fees at one month's wage, or RM1,700, Bangladeshi workers, for example, routinely pay recruitment fees of between RM20,000 and RM30,000.
"That is nearly 12 to 17 times the legal limit, forcing workers to overstay to recoup their payment."
Santiago called for the recruitment-fee system to be dismantled, a mandatory employer-pays principle to be enforced, and binding bilateral labour agreements to be established with labour-sending countries.
Malaysia, one of Southeast Asia's more developed economies, relies heavily on migrant workers to fill labour shortages in sectors including construction, plantations and services.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OhBulan! Paling Viral Online returns with four new categories
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:
OhBulan! Paling Viral Online returns in November with four new categories following its inaugural edition in 2025. The awards give fans more opportunities to recognise their favourite celebrities, content creators and personalities through online voting.
The second edition will feature nine categories, including Pelakon Paling Viral, Penyanyi Gen Z Paling Viral, Peniaga Paling Viral and Nepo Baby Paling Viral. The Pelakon Paling Viral category will combine male and female actors, with one winner selected.
Five categories from the inaugural edition will also return: Content Creator Paling Viral, Filem Paling Viral, Drama Paling Viral, Lagu Paling HOT and Kelab Peminat Paling Viral.
Voting will take place in two phases — Top 15 and Top 5 — to determine the winners in each category. The Top 15 phase runs from Nov 2 to Dec 1, with the results determining which 15 nominees advance to the next round, while the Top 5 phase runs from Dec 7 to Jan 8, allowing fans to vote for their preferred nominees from the remaining contenders.
Fans can cast up to 50 votes a day throughout the voting period.
OhBulan! editorial content lead Noor Zulaikha Yusof said the encouraging response to the inaugural edition had prompted the return of the awards.
"Following the encouraging response to our first edition, we wanted to continue OhBulan! Paling Viral Online 2.0 to recognise celebrities, content creators, entrepreneurs, songs and dramas that have captured public attention," she said.
"We introduced four new categories to give more people the chance to be recognised, while keeping a special category dedicated to fans to appreciate their continued support. We believe that with everyone's backing, this edition will make an even greater impact," she added.
The winners will be announced during a live broadcast on OhBulan!'s official TikTok account on Jan 15 at 9pm.
Further information about the awards and voting is available on the
official website
.

Title: Malaysia-Switzerland trade hits RM13.4bil: Johari Ghani
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia-Switzerland economic ties continue to grow, with bilateral trade reaching RM13.4 billion in 2025, an increase of 9.8 per cent from the previous year.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said as of June 2026, 211 manufacturing projects with Swiss participation had been implemented in Malaysia, involving investments worth RM12.8 billion and creating 19,744 jobs.
He welcomed more quality investments that could strengthen local industrial capabilities and create high-skilled job opportunities for Malaysians.
"We also discussed the Malaysia-European Free Trade Association Economic Partnership Agreement (Meepa) and efforts to strengthen investment cooperation.
"I emphasised the importance of implementing Meepa to expand market access and create more opportunities for businesses in both countries.
"This was alongside reaffirming Malaysia's commitment to sustainable industrial and trade development," he said in a Facebook post today.
He also shared photographs of himself receiving a courtesy call from Switzerland's state secretary for economic affairs Helene Budliger Artieda at his office here.
Johari said the meeting provided an opportunity to strengthen trade and investment cooperation, particularly in advanced manufacturing, precision engineering and medical technology.
