Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected in 12 states, KL this evening, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 12 states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather in the Peninsula would affect the whole of Melaka and eight districts in Johor, namely Kluang, Pontian, Kulai, Johor Bahru, Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat, Tangkak and Muar.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Kuala Muda, Kulim, Baling, Sik, Padang Terap, Pendang and Pokok Sena, while in Penang, the warning covers Seberang Perai Utara.
The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Larut Matang and Selama, and in Kelantan, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu and Bachok.
In Terengganu, the areas affected are Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman and Kuala Nerus, while in Pahang, the warning covers Jerantut, Rompin and Bentong. In Selangor, it covers Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Hulu Langat and Petaling, while in Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Jelebu, Seremban, Kuala Pilah, Rembau and Tampin.
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, the affected areas are Kuching (Bau and Kuching), Serian, Sarikei (Sarikei, Maradong and Pakan), Betong (Kabong and Saratok), Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Samarahan, Sri Aman (Pantu and Lingga), Mukah (Daro, Tanjung Manis and Matu), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Sipitang, Tambunan, Keningau, Sook, Membakut, Beaufort and Tenom), the West Coast (Ranau, Papar, Penampang, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu and Tuaran), Kudat (Kota Marudu) and Sandakan (Telupid). — Bernama

Title: Nilai border control officer’s death: Police record statements from 18 individuals, husband remains in remand until Oct 22
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Police have recorded statements from 18 individuals to assist in investigations into the death of an officer of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor in the near future.
“The suspect, who is the victim’s husband and is in his 30s, remains in remand until October 22 to assist in investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“Checks also revealed that the man has 16 previous criminal and drug-related records,” he told Bernama here today.
Alzafny said the post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure applied to her neck. The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.
The victim, who was in her 30s, was found dead after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband at the quarters, reportedly following a misunderstanding.
Police received a report on the incident at 9.30pm after the victim’s husband turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported the death. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 debate: Muhyiddin calls for urban poverty master plan, MP allocation law proposed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Issues concerning urban poverty, the allocation of funds for Members of Parliament (MPs), and efforts to strengthen the nation’s healthcare sector were among the topics raised during the policy-level debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin (PN-Pagoh) proposed that the government establish a dedicated master plan to address poverty in urban and semi-urban areas over a five-year period, utilising an integrated approach that involves various ministries.
The former prime minister said the plan should focus on housing, healthcare, employment, education, skills training, and social assistance to ensure that low-income groups also benefit from the nation’s economic development.
“A specific plan must be formulated to ensure that the urban poor gain access to economic and educational opportunities, enabling them to improve their own lives and those of their families through the spillover effects of urban development,” he said.
He added that development planning in major cities such as Kuala Lumpur, Penang, and Johor Bahru must incorporate poverty eradication efforts, particularly by providing economic and educational opportunities for low-income populations.
Meanwhile, Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) proposed the enactment of a Parliamentary Constituency Development Allocation Act to ensure that all Members of Parliament, regardless of their political affiliation, receive allocations on an equitable basis.
He said the drafting of the act could be carried out by the Parliamentary Service Council, following the enforcement of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025.
“This is for the benefit of all citizens. I hope that Parliament (the Parliamentary Service Council) can initiate the process of drafting the act,” he said.
Meanwhile, P. Prabakaran (PH-Batu) expressed support for the government’s move to offer permanent positions to over 9,000 contract doctors next year.
However, he emphasised that the government must ensure clearer career paths and sufficient training opportunities, while also addressing the welfare of all healthcare workers specifically regarding their workload and work-life balance.
“At the same time, the public continues to face challenges in obtaining treatment at government health clinics and hospitals, including long waiting times, overcrowding, and difficulties in accessing specialist care.
“Therefore, I suggest that the government assess the need to increase the number of doctors, nurses, and healthcare personnel, based on the local population size and patient load at each healthcare facility,” he said.
Prabakaran added that the government should also focus on hospital bed capacity, the maintenance of medical equipment, and the upgrading of existing facilities, in addition to strengthening primary healthcare services and early disease screening. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak steps up preparations to co-host 2027 SEA Games
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 20 — Sarawak is intensifying preparations to co-host the 2027 SEA Games from September 18 to 29 next year, with promotional activities set to continue across the state, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was told today.
Sarawak Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the promotional activities include a torch run covering all 12 divisions in the state.
He said the initiative would extend the excitement of the Games beyond Kuching and provide communities across the state with an opportunity to be part of the historic event.
“On September 18 this year, Sarawak marked the one-year countdown to SEA Games 2027 with a special ceremony to mark key milestones in our preparations.
“The ceremony also provided an opportunity to introduce the Games to the public and raise awareness of Sarawak’s role as co-host. The official SEA Games Sarawak website was also launched to provide the public and media with information and updates on the Games,” he said when winding up the debate for his ministry.
Abdul Karim said Sarawak will host 18 of the 43 sports at the 2027 SEA Games, with dance sport newly included in the Sarawak cluster.
Meanwhile, commenting on the 2026 Malaysia Games, he said the Sarawak government would award cash incentives of RM15,000 to athletes who won gold medals, RM5,000 to silver medallists and RM3,000 to bronze medallists.
Athletes who broke records would also receive an additional RM1,000 incentive in recognition of their outstanding performances and achievements. — Bernama

Title: Sabah CM: RM150m Nabawan police headquarters, housing project to begin in January 2027
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 20 — The construction of the Nabawan district police headquarters (IPD) and police housing project, with an allocation ceiling of RM150 million, is expected to begin in January 2027, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the infrastructure project aimed to strengthen security capabilities, law enforcement and service delivery to the public, particularly in Nabawan and surrounding areas.
He added that the project must be implemented with integrity and in compliance with the stipulated specifications and standards to ensure maximum benefits for the public and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel.
“We do not merely want to see this project completed, but also want to ensure that it delivers long-term benefits,” he said in a statement after officiating the groundbreaking ceremony for the Nabawan IPD and police housing project today.
Also present were Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, Sabah State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman and Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.
Hajiji said the construction of the Nabawan IPD was crucial given the district’s strategic location along the border with Indonesia, which required stronger security capabilities to address cross-border crime and illegal activities.
He said these threats called for integrated, effective and continuous enforcement efforts, including strengthening the PDRM in terms of personnel, infrastructure, operational facilities and administrative systems.
According to Hajiji, the Nabawan police station, established in 1976, currently comes under the administration of the Keningau IPD, although Nabawan has an administrative area of about 6,089 square kilometres.
“Given the size of the administrative area, the need for a more structured policing system suited to current security demands warrants serious attention.
“The development of the Nabawan IPD is an important step towards strengthening the police presence and policing capabilities in the area,” he said.
Hajiji also described the project as a manifestation of the government’s unwavering concern for the welfare, comfort and safety of front-line personnel.
“Providing a conducive infrastructure equipped with the latest technological facilities is no longer a luxury, but a critical necessity, particularly in border areas,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia looks to put durians on the fast track to China by road, rail in three to four days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is stepping up negotiations with several countries in the region to facilitate the export of fresh durians to China by road and rail, with shipments expected to take just three to four days, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the initiative was aimed at providing a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to air freight, which is expensive, and sea transport, which takes considerably longer.
He said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) was working closely with the Foreign Ministry and Transport Ministry to coordinate cross-border routes through Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia.
“Overland shipments are expected to take only three to four days, allowing goods, particularly durians, to reach the Chinese market quickly. Malaysian durians are very popular among consumers in China, but sometimes they find it difficult to obtain them at more affordable prices,” he said when replying to a supplementary question from Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng).
Mohamad added that formal negotiations to secure transit rights began on July 20 to pave the way for the proposed route through the four countries. — Bernama

Title: States urged to gazette over 15,000ha of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia, FT
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — More than 15,000 hectares or 64.47 per cent of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories have not yet been gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said all state governments have been urged to expedite the gazettement of public open spaces to ensure designated green areas remain protected and are fully utilised for the benefit of the people, particularly by providing green spaces in densely populated areas.
He said 23,297.15 hectares of public open spaces have been identified in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories as of December 2025. However, only 35.53 per cent, or 8,278.44 hectares, have been gazetted so far.
“Another 15,018.72 hectares, equivalent to 64.47 per cent, have yet to be gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement. This situation requires attention and follow-up action by state governments to expedite the process in line with the Malaysia Madani sustainable environmental development agenda,” he said in a statement here today.
Nga said public open spaces are not merely areas for leisure and recreation but also important assets that contribute to the well-being of the people.
He said such spaces also serve as green zones that absorb surface runoff, helping to reduce the risk of flash floods, while providing recreational areas that improve the community’s quality of life.
He said gazettement is crucial to protect public open spaces from encroachment, inappropriate changes in land use, as well as management and maintenance issues that could compromise users’ safety.
As such, he called on state governments to intensify gazettement efforts in accordance with Section 62 of the National Land Code [Act 828], as the matter falls under the jurisdiction of state governments.
“The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), through PLANMalaysia, will continue to monitor the gazettement status of public open spaces in collaboration with relevant parties to support more sustainable, liveable urban development that prioritises the well-being of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MARA says all 242 sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid the unrest.
Its deputy director-general (Education) Zahari Aziz said all 242 students were safe, based on the latest reports from student representatives at their respective universities, and none had been reported to have been involved in the unrest.
“Academic activities are continuing as usual. In areas experiencing public transport disruptions, the universities have taken appropriate measures to conduct classes online,” he said in a statement today.
He said MARA, through its overseas office in Frankfurt, Germany, remained in close contact with the students and had reminded them to stay alert and avoid areas where demonstrations were taking place.
The students had also been advised to follow instructions issued by the local authorities and the Malaysian Embassy in Paris, he said.
“MARA would continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Queen calls for long-term measures to protect students from haze
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
Her Majesty stressed the urgent need for a coordinated response, emphasising long-term strategies rather than temporary measures introduced only during haze emergencies.
“Collective action, particularly from the government and private sector, is needed to plan proactive measures to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
“Close cooperation from local communities is also essential to strengthen the effectiveness of home-based teaching and learning (PdPR).
“Relevant parties must also develop long-term strategic plans rather than relying solely on temporary solutions when haze emergencies occur,” Her Majesty said.
The royal message was shared in a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page.
The Queen delivered the message in connection with an audience involving the Johor government, parents and educators on haze-related issues and schooling at the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) Tower, yesterday.
The session reflected Her Majesty’s concern for the well-being and education of the younger generation.
Her Highness Che’ Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present.
In the same message, the Queen also expressed her appreciation to Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah and Jeffrey Cheah Foundation for contributing face masks for schoolchildren in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Her Majesty also commended Tan Sri Patrick Yeoh and YTL Communications for providing SIM cards to support students’ access to digital learning, and thanked other partners who had contributed to the welfare of schoolchildren.
The audience was also attended by State Secretary Datuk Mohammed Ridha Abd Kadir and State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
Representatives from state and federal departments, teachers, parents, Bangsa Johor Bahagia (BJB) residents and People’s Housing Programme (PPR) communities were also present. — Bernama

Title: Govt discusses measures to tackle glut of imported vegetables hurting local farmers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS) is in discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) to find effective measures to address the glut of imported vegetables, which is affecting local producers.
Its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the discussions also took into account the implementation of the requirement to submit a Certificate of Analysis (CoA), which became mandatory on June 1, 2026, although some views held that the measure was still insufficient.
“We have brought this matter up for discussion at the food security level, and we are analysing what new measures need to be introduced to protect the position of vegetable growers in Malaysia, as well as those involved in fruit production,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards.
Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS).
He said commodities facing oversupply included chillies, cabbage, round cabbage, mustard greens, tomatoes and cucumbers, prompting complaints from local growers, including those in Cameron Highlands and Johor.
In response to Wong’s original question on the performance of myGAP certification since the introduction of e-myGAP in 2020, Mohamad said the system was introduced to shorten the certification period from two years to 90 working days without compromising compliance with Malaysian Standards (MS).
However, he said the timeframe depended on the farm’s level of readiness and the applicant’s compliance with all stipulated certification requirements.
Based on records, Mohamad said the number of applications increased from 2,507 in 2021 to 3,652 in 2025, while 3,282 applications were recorded for 2026 as of the reporting cut-off.
Of these, the number of applications successfully certified in less than 90 working days stood at 324 in 2021, 163 in 2022, 183 in 2023, 373 in 2024, 249 in 2025 and 206 in 2026.
However, he said most applications still took more than 90 working days to process, involving 2,097 applications in 2021, 1,895 in 2022, 3,277 in 2023, 2,967 in 2024 and 3,106 in 2025. This was partly due to the need to carry out corrective actions to address identified non-compliance.
Meanwhile, responding to a supplementary question from Nurul Amin Hamid (PN-Padang Terap) on market preference for myGAP-certified produce and guidance for smallholders, Mohamad said the Department of Agriculture would assist farm operators in obtaining certification once applications had been submitted.
He said the ministry had also asked the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) to intervene in marketing agricultural produce when oversupply caused selling prices to fall below production costs.
“This happens when, for example, the selling prices of chillies, okra or other crops fall too low, below production costs. We then ask Fama to intervene so that farmers and small-scale vegetable growers do not incur losses when there is an oversupply in the market,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia to expand online child safety cooperation, seek Singapore’s involvement
Article:
BALI, Oct 20 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address online child safety issues, with efforts also planned to involve Singapore in the collaboration.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said online safety, particularly involving children, was an important issue requiring the collective attention of countries in the region.
“We are working towards holding a trilateral meeting involving Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore, Insha’Allah, in December, if schedules permit,” he told Bernama after a bilateral meeting with his Indonesian counterpart, Meutya Hafid, here on Tuesday.
He said that although Asean countries have different laws and implementation approaches, the initiative by Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore could encourage other countries in the region to participate.
“We not only have aligned policies, but may also have several similar mechanisms, although they may not be exactly the same,” he explained.
Fahmi also welcomed Meutya’s intention to strengthen cooperation between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Indonesia’s Communication and Digital Affairs Ministry.
MCMC’s experience in handling public complaints related to social media could also be useful to the Indonesian authorities, he added.
In a related development, Singapore’s Digital Development and Information Minister Josephine Teo said she and Fahmi had exchanged views on developments in their respective telecommunications sectors during an impromptu meeting at Ngurah Rai International Airport on Monday.
In a post on her official social media account, Teo said the discussions included quantum-safe communications, as well as online safety for children and young people.
She also expressed hope of hosting Fahmi in Singapore in the near future.
Teo happened to meet Fahmi, who had just arrived in Bali, while she was waiting for her flight back to Singapore after attending Bali Tech Week 2026.
Fahmi is in Bali at the invitation of the organisers to deliver a keynote address at Bali Tech Week.
He was accompanied by MCMC Deputy Managing Director (Regulatory) Datuk Dr Mohamed Sulaiman Sultan Suhaibudden and First Secretary (Economics) at the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta, Fakhrul Arifin Mohammad Zulkifly. — Bernama

Title: Anwar cites cases of corporate owners forced to sell firms over political interference
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government inherited a system lacking transparency, allowing corporate crimes and market manipulation to go largely unchecked for decades, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said weaknesses in the previous system meant enforcement action was rarely taken in major cases involving billions of ringgit in losses, including corporate takeovers and banking transactions allegedly influenced by political interference.
Anwar alleged that several cases involving so-called corporate mafia activities were linked to a former finance minister who wielded considerable influence and controlled substantial financial resources.
“We inherited a system that lacked transparency. Members of Parliament who have followed developments since the 1980s and 1990s would know how major companies, such as Multi-Purpose Holdings Bhd (MPHB), were allegedly forced to be sold to a group led by Datuk Seri Akbar Khan.
“All this was linked to the former finance minister at the time, who had considerable influence and financial resources,” he said in reply to Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) during Ministers’ Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Aminuddin had sought an update on alleged corporate mafia activities involving legal violations and the enforcement action taken.
Anwar also cited several other cases which, he said, underscored the need for enforcement agencies, including Bank Negara Malaysia, the Securities Commission (SC), Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the police, to carry out their duties transparently.
“RHB Bank was successfully managed by Tan Sri Rashid Hussain, but he was forced to relinquish his stake and eventually lost control. Those who subsequently held ownership were also linked to the former finance minister.
“Phileo Allied Bank was among the fastest-growing banks at the time, but the former finance minister directed banks to consolidate. It was subsequently relinquished because of the former minister’s interests in Langkah Bahagia Sdn Bhd, which later acquired a stake in the company,” he alleged.
Anwar also said the SC had increased enforcement action in corporate crime cases by two to three times since 2023 compared with previous years. — Bernama

Title: Govt to consolidate MAF veterans’ associations to improve aid distribution, says Adly Zahari
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) plans to streamline and consolidate more than 300 registered Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans’ associations to facilitate the distribution of assistance to the group, said its Deputy Minister Adly Zahari.
He said under the initiative, to be implemented by the National Veterans Council and the Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), the number of associations would be reduced to 100, with the associations operating under parent associations to enable government assistance schemes to be coordinated more effectively.
“At the same time, the ministry is also considering increasing the contributions or allocations that we have provided.
“We also hope the state governments will continue to support and encourage veterans’ associations, as JHEV’s focus is on ensuring the welfare of veterans,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Commander (Rtd) Nordin Ahmad Ismail (PN-Lumut), who wanted to know what steps the ministry or JHEV was taking to coordinate the registration of veterans’ associations with state governments.
In response to a supplementary question from RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) on the possibility of re-employing veterans at the country’s main entry points, Adly said the government had begun recruiting veterans into the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) this year.
“When AKPS recruits veterans, we can shorten the training process by up to six months because they already have expertise in national defence.
“Similarly, air force veterans with technical expertise can be readily absorbed into the defence industry,” he said.
Adly said the ministry had also allocated funds under Budget 2026 and Budget 2027 to enable former military personnel to be recruited as forest rangers.
He said the move would not only help reduce government expenditure but also make use of veterans’ expertise in the security sector and safeguard national sovereignty. — Bernama

Title: No quota for CLP exam passes, candidates assessed purely on merit, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Candidates sitting the Certificate in Legal Practice (CLP) examination are assessed purely on merit, with no quota imposed on the number of passes, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said candidates were assessed based on their performance, with a minimum passing mark set for each subject.
“The passing mark for each CLP subject is 40, and there is no quota for passes. Candidates are assessed purely on merit,” he said during the question-and-answer session.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Dr V. Sivakumar (PH-Batu Gajah) on measures to address the low CLP examination pass rate while maintaining professional standards, after only 19 per cent of candidates (158 out of 826) obtained a full pass in 2026, compared with 21 per cent in 2025.
Kulasegaran clarified that the statistics covered only the main 2026 CLP examination and did not include the results of the supplementary examination.
“The overall results of the 2026 CLP examination will be announced in November 2026, after the results of the supplementary examination have been obtained and approved by the Board,” he said.
On the factors contributing to candidates’ failure, Kulasegaran said most candidates were law graduates from the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, where they had studied the common law system, but appeared not to have adequately prepared for the Malaysian law component of the CLP examination.
He said that candidates also had difficulty identifying legal issues in examination questions, applying the law to the facts and citing relevant case law to support their answers.
In response to Sivakumar’s original question on the CLP’s structure, assessment methods, duration of study and transition to the New Bar Course (NBC), Kulasegaran said the Legal Profession Qualifying Board had established an NBC Task Force on April 27.
He said the task force was tasked with conducting a study to develop an implementation framework for the NBC, including arrangements to ensure a smooth transition to the new professional legal qualification system.
Kulasegaran said the NBC, which would replace the CLP, comprises two programmes, namely the Conversion Course (CC) and the Legal Practice Postgraduate Certificate (LPPC), with a greater emphasis on practical legal skills and professional competence.
He said the existing CLP system assesses candidates solely through written examinations, without a comprehensive evaluation of their practical legal skills, and does not require them to complete preparatory courses before sitting the examinations.
On the transition from the CLP to the NBC, he explained that the NBC Task Force was reviewing policies concerning candidates who had yet to pass the existing examinations but still had remaining attempts and valid registration periods.
“The qualifying board will consider this matter once the NBC Task Force has completed its study on the transition mechanism,” he said.
Responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Che Mohamad Zulkifly Jusoh (PN-Besut) on checks and balances in setting the curriculum and assessing prospective lawyers, Kulasegaran said the professional legal qualification system would continue under an improved approach with a revised set of courses.
He said that the improvements took into account complaints about the previous system while emphasising the difference between academic legal studies and the professional training required to become a lawyer.
Kulasegaran explained that law programmes in the United Kingdom and several other countries typically take three years to complete, compared with four years at local universities, where a professional component is introduced in the fourth year. — Bernama

Title: Loke wants Transport Expo Asia to become permanent biennial event, next edition in 2028
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke wants Transport Expo Asia (TXA) to become a permanent biennial event, with the next edition set for 2028 to showcase transport technologies and innovation.
He said the exhibition would bring together industry players, promote international best practices and support the development of Malaysia’s transport industry.
“I hope that TXA will be organised once every two years,” he said when opening the expo at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) today.
Also present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and Transport Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan.
Held from Oct 20 to 22, TXA 2026 serves as a key meeting point for the land, aviation, maritime and logistics sectors.
Loke said the idea for a dedicated transport exhibition emerged from the ministry’s co-organising of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA).
He said LIMA’s growing popularity and increasingly constrained exhibition space prompted the ministry to consider holding its own event, while allowing LIMA to focus more on the defence industry.
“I brought a proposal to the Cabinet two years ago for the ministry to branch out from LIMA, leading to an inaugural TXA event on a smaller scale last year,” he said.
This year’s exhibition features 410 exhibitors and technology innovators, providing a platform to connect public policy with industry innovation and translate collaboration into improved transport services, stronger trade links and new economic opportunities.
Loke said the technologies on show across the 15,000-square-metre exhibition hall, alongside autonomous vehicle demonstrations and strategic agreements, were expected to bring tangible improvements in efficiency, emissions reduction, safety and reliability.
Speaking to reporters after the opening ceremony, Loke said government spending on transport infrastructure and maintenance should create more opportunities for Malaysian companies across the supply chain.
He said original equipment manufacturers and suppliers could use TXA to connect with local businesses, helping government expenditure support domestic manufacturing and component supply.
“Rail, aviation and road transport require extensive supply chains, creating opportunities for Malaysian companies to supply components and support maintenance activities,” he said.
On the expo’s economic impact, Loke said no target had been set for its first large-scale edition. However, several memoranda of understanding and agreements are expected to be signed during the three-day event.
He encouraged logistics companies and transport-related small and medium enterprises (SMEs)to explore the technologies on display and pursue potential business opportunities. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, WHO aim to finalise pandemic agreement by May 2027, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysia and the World Health Organization (WHO) have renewed their joint commitment to finalise the landmark WHO Pandemic Agreement by May 2027, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said Malaysia is emphasising the need to strike a balance between intellectual property rights protection and equitable access to medical countermeasures during health emergencies.
Dzulkefly said this was among the key issues he discussed with WHO director-general Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus during a courtesy call on the sidelines of the 77th session of the WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific (WPRO), held in Manila, from Oct 19 to 22.
“WHO also expressed strong confidence in Malaysia by inviting the country to play a strategic leadership role in the Western Pacific region, working alongside regional countries to build global consensus on emergency preparedness,” he said in a Facebook post today.
During the meeting, he said Malaysia also reiterated its firm commitment to supporting sustainable financing for WHO.
“Meanwhile, Dr Tedros’ appreciation of the progress made in Malaysia’s ongoing primary healthcare (PHC) transformation efforts was a great source of encouragement for Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Suhakam calls for femicide to be recognised in law, tougher action on gender-based violence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has urged the government to recognise femicide in the country’s legal framework. It described femicide as the most extreme form of gender-based violence against women and girls.
“Such violence extends beyond individual acts of criminal conduct and reflects broader patterns of discrimination, gender inequality and shortcomings in preventing and addressing violence against women and girls,” it said in a statement today.
The commission described femicide as “a preventable human rights violation requiring stronger laws, early intervention, accessible protection mechanisms and coordinated action”.
“Recognising their gender-related nature is essential to understanding the underlying causes, identifying risks and strengthening prevention, protection and accountability measures,” it said.
The call follows a briefing on October 15 by Suhakam commissioner Melissa Mohd Akhir to the Parliamentary Select Committee on Women, Children and Community Development.
The committee is chaired by Puchong MP Yeo Bee Yin.
Suhakam said “preventing femicide requires action before violence escalates into the loss of life”.
It called for existing laws to be reviewed so femicide is recognised as a distinct form of gender-based violence. It also asked for a national body to coordinate and monitor efforts against such violence at federal, state and local levels, backed by better data collection.
It also urged safer cities and communities through better street lighting, safer public transport, accessible reporting mechanisms and secure schools. It asked media organisations and digital platforms to curb victim-blaming and content that normalises gender-based violence.
The commission said sufficient funding was needed for shelters, psychosocial services, legal aid and women’s organisations, particularly in rural and underserved communities.
Citing Article 8(2) of the Federal Constitution and Malaysia’s obligations under the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (Cedaw), Suhakam said the government must pursue a policy of eliminating discrimination against women without delay.
Marking the International Day of the Girl Child this month, the commission said “every woman and girl has the right to live free from violence and fear, and that safeguarding this right is a shared responsibility of the government and society”.

Title: Johor-Singapore RTS Link fares expected by year-end, says transport minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Fares for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link are expected to be announced by the end of this year, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
The announcement will be made ahead of the service’s planned opening in February next year.
“The announcement would be made jointly with RTS Operations (RTSO), as the project was a bilateral initiative between Malaysia and Singapore.
“I cannot make any unilateral announcement because it is a bilateral project,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He said the fare announcement would be made before the service begins operating to give the public sufficient time to familiarise themselves with the ticket prices.
In a joint statement made on October 2, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore and the Malaysian Transport Ministry said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline.
The service was previously expected to commence in January. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.

Title: Anthony Loke: Bus ticket policy targets overseas online agents, not operators
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government’s policy to channel bus ticket sales through licensed terminals is meant to restrict online ticketing agents (OTA).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said operators needed to understand the policy and there will be a session to explain it to them.
“The policy is not intended to cause losses to bus companies.
“What we want to restrict is the role of online ticketing agents (OTAs), many of which are based overseas.
“They sell tickets and collect commissions but do not provide services at the terminals or manage terminal operations,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today.
He cited situations when a problem relating to cancellation or delay in bus services, the ministry is not able to regulate these issues.
“When problems arise, such as service failures or refund disputes, we have limited ability to regulate these agents.
“We are introducing this measure to ensure ticket sales, terminal management and ticketing operations are better regulated,” he added.
Loke stressed that there should be no financial losses for bus operators, at the same time ensuring that terminals cannot charge more than their existing rates.
“In fact, we hope terminals can reduce their charges and provide better returns for bus operators,” he said.
In this case, Loke said, transactions will be business-to-business (B2B), between the terminals and bus operators.
“The government is responsible for the policy decision, while the commercial arrangements will be handled directly by the parties involved.
Loke’s comments come after a new ruling by the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) was announced whereby express bus tickets were to be sold only through licensed terminals from November 1.
According to the circular issued to bus operators, it involves granting terminals exclusive rights to sell tickets and introduce new commercial fee structure.
However, APAD said tickets could still be purchased through OTAs or bus operators' websites if the terminals were owned by the operators themselves.

Title: Anwar says Siti Nurhaliza personally invited him to concert, praises cultural heritage showcase
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said his attendance at national songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza’s concert recently was by special invitation and also in support of efforts to promote local arts, heritage and culture.
Responding to criticism from several quarters over his attendance, Anwar thanked them and said he accepted their views with an open heart, according to a report by national news agency Bernama today.
“I went because Siti Nurhaliza and her husband, Datuk K (Datuk Seri Khalid Mohamad Jiwa), really urged me to attend, although I arrived a little late... but I was criticised by several quarters. Thank you,” he said during Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar was responding to a joke by Mohd Sany Hamzan (PH-Hulu Langat) about his attendance at the Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara, held at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil last Saturday.
The prime minister said the concert by the country’s renowned singer deserved praise for elevating the nation’s cultural heritage through its various traditional elements.
He said the traditional concert showcased the beauty of the country’s artistic heritage through
wayang kulit
, traditional dances and cultural performances from Sabah and Sarawak, highlighting the richness of local heritage and classical songs.

Title: Johor businessman says identity misused in fake Facebook account insulting King, Malays
Article:
SEGAMAT, Oct 20 — A businessman has claimed that a fake Facebook account, using his name and image, was used to post content insulting the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Malay community.
Segamat police chief Superintendent Mohd Jumazanzahir Chek Ismail said that the complainant, a local man, lodged a police report here the day before yesterday.
“Police confirm having received a report regarding the misuse of his personal information to create a fake Facebook account.
“This account used his name and photo to upload posts involving 3R (religion, race, and the royal institution) issues,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Jumazanzahir said the complainant has denied that the Facebook account belongs to him and maintains that he never posted the content in question.
“He believes his personal information was misused, creating the false impression that he was the individual responsible for publishing such content," he said, adding that two police reports have been filed in this district, with another lodged in the Shah Alam, all related to the issue.
Meanwhile, Mohd Jumazanzahir advised the public against misusing the identities or personal information of others for fake accounts, disseminating seditious content, or inciting misunderstandings within the community.
“The public is also advised to refrain from speculating or resharing content that has not been verified, particularly content that touches upon sensitive issues regarding race, religion, and the royal institution," he said.
Previously, a post circulating on social media, using the name Cher Cher, had insulted the Yang di-Pertuan Agong through the use of edited content, accompanied by a caption insulting the Malay community.

Title: Azmin: RoS deregistration shows Perikatan leadership breached coalition constitution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the cancellation of Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) registration showed that the coalition’s leadership, led by PAS, had breached the Societies Act 1966 and PN’s constitution.
In a statement posted on Facebook today, Azmin said the explanations and evidence provided by PAS during the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) investigation were baseless and failed to meet legal and constitutional requirements.
He said the PN leadership’s decision to deny Bersatu the right to attend, express its views and vote at a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16 amounted to a serious breach of Clause 7.1 of the coalition’s constitution.
Azmin said the action had caused significant harm to PN and could jeopardise its future.
He also accused the coalition’s leadership of disregarding good governance and transparency, creating pressure to remove Bersatu’s membership through a veto exercised by an individual who did not hold a position on the PN Supreme Council.
Azmin said Bersatu had been called to give evidence to the RoS on August 18 and had provided factual explanations and evidence that PN’s leadership had denied the party rights guaranteed under the coalition’s constitution.
He said Bersatu’s complaint, submitted on August 11, was intended to ensure PN was managed with accountability, transparency and integrity, and complied with the law and its constitution.
“PN cannot be allowed to become a shelter for groups hungry for political power and seeking to hijack the Perikatan Nasional brand, which is moderate, progressive and responsive to the Malaysian people,” he said.
Azmin accused PAS and its allies of portraying themselves as victims of political manoeuvring to gain sympathy ahead of the Melaka state election.
He also criticised what he described as excessive identity politics, accusing PAS of failing to manage an organisation based on democratic principles and good governance, and of betraying its political allies.
Azmin said Bersatu found the RoS decision difficult to accept because it was a founding member of PN and had helped establish the coalition.
Nevertheless, he said Bersatu accepted that PN must fulfil its responsibilities under its constitution and the Societies Act 1966, also known as Act 832, to ensure legal compliance and orderly governance.
He said Bersatu would study the full RoS decision before its Supreme Leadership Council discussed the next steps to rebuild public confidence in a political coalition that promotes moderation, values-based politics and a new vision for a prosperous Malaysia.

Title: Perikatan to challenge RoS deregistration, appeal to home minister, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will challenge the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to cancel the coalition’s registration, including by appealing to the home minister, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today.
He said the legal challenge would begin with an application during the Kuala Lumpur High Court hearing of PN’s application for a stay on Thursday.
Takiyuddin said Section 18 of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832) allows any local society, office-bearer, member or aggrieved party to appeal against a decision by the RoS to the Home Minister.
The appeal must be filed within 30 days of the RoS decision, he said, adding that Section 8 of the same Act empowers the Home Minister to confirm, reject or amend the Registrar’s decision, with the minister’s decision being final.
“PN will challenge the validity of the Cancellation Order and seek a stay of its implementation and all its effects pending the court’s determination.
“PN also urges the Attorney General to explain this action in light of the position taken by the Attorney General’s Chambers in court during the hearing of PN’s stay application this Thursday,” he told a press conference at Parliament today.
Takiyuddin said PN would also take action against parties it believed had shown contempt for the court process.
“PN will also take action against all parties that have shown contempt for and disregarded the court process,” he said.
(RoS) cancelled the registration of PN after finding that the explanation submitted by the coalition failed to refute the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.
RoS said it made the decision after examining all the documents and explanations submitted by PN on October 12.
According to the department, the reasons given by PN also did not provide strong justification for maintaining the party’s registration.

Title: Govt looking at tougher penalties to tackle cable theft across public transport sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Transport Ministry is in the midst of drafting necessary measures that look into increasing penalties for action against cable theft affecting public transport operators, including the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL).
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the proposed amendments would not be limited to ECRL, as cable theft was a problem affecting operators across the sector.
“Proposals to increase penalties for cable theft must go through parliamentary process.
“We are currently drafting the necessary measures,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He however said operators must also strengthen preventive measures, warning that tougher penalties alone would not resolve the problem if effective prevention was not in place.
“Whatever penalties are imposed, if preventive measures are not implemented effectively, they will not solve the problem,” he said.
The minister said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and other operators were exploring additional ways to prevent cable theft, including the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance and other technologies.
He added cable theft was not unique to Malaysia, but also affected transport operators in other parts of the world.
“I encourage companies and start-ups to develop innovative solutions to address the problem, including through research and development.
“This is how exhibitions such as TXA could provide a platform for companies to present solutions to operational challenges faced by transport operators,” he said.
Yesterday, the police busted four gangs suspected of cable theft belonging to ECRL and Telekom Malaysia (TM).

Title: Anwar: Madani anti-money laundering enforcement actions net RM4b up to 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysian enforcement agencies have frozen up to RM4.3 billion in funds and 2.1 million shares up to 2026 as part of ongoing anti-money laundering operations, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament today, citing police enforcement statistics.
Anwar said his government has stepped up efforts to crack down on white-collar crime, which resulted in billions of ringgit seized and hundreds of prosecutions.
Between 2022 to September 2026, the Securities Commission has initiated 239 criminal charges against 50 individuals or entities compared to just 76 charges against 33 individuals or entities during the same period from 2017 to 2021.
“The total number of criminal charges has increased more than threefold,” Anwar, who is also finance minister, said during PM Question Time.
The network of corporate crime cases that have been rampant includes criminal acquisition and takeover of companies listed on Bursa Malaysia as well as private companies, stock market manipulation, violations of corporate disclosure and regulatory laws, and illegal money-lending activities, he added.
The government had seized an additional RM1 billion along with 2.1 million shares during the same period, while other enforcement actions further resulted in RM48 million in forfeited assets and RM1.1 billion in financial compounds issued to offenders.
“An additional sum of more than RM3 billion remains subject to ongoing court forfeiture proceedings aimed at recovering assets for the government,” Anwar said.

Title: Finance Ministry halts selected pre-qualified tender method for new Rural and Regional Development Ministry projects after audit findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has halted approvals for the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) to use the Selected Pre-Qualified Open Tender (TTPKT) method for new projects following findings in the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2025.
The ministry said the TTPKT method was introduced in 2023 as a special procedure to expedite the implementation of high-impact projects for the public and remained in place until June 30, 2025, with several enhancements aimed at strengthening government procurement governance.
“However, the Auditor-General’s Report 2/2025 found that that the implementation of the TTPKT method, including by the KKDW, had not achieved the government’s original objectives,” the ministry said in a written reply published on Parliament’s portal.
The ministry was responding to a question from Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) regarding action against KKDW officials responsible for authorising spending that exceeded allocations by RM2.1 billion between 2023 and 2025, as well as whether the contractors involved had been appointed through open tender.
According to the MOF, contractors for the Rural Road Programme under the KKDW are generally selected through tender processes, including open tender and the TTPKT method.
The ministry said the KKDW had, over the past few years, made financial commitments and incurred expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved in the annual budgets for rural road projects, resulting in arrears and delays in payments to contractors.
In this regard, the MOF said it had taken additional measures, including directing the KKDW to suspend the issuance of new Letters of Acceptance (SST) for rural road projects on September 10.
The ministry said it had also approved an additional RM500 million in expenditure for 2026 through a letter authorising expenditure beyond the approved allocation, after savings were identified in other ministries’ development expenditure.
In addition, the MOF said it had asked the KKDW to prepare projections of funding requirements for rural road projects up to the end of 2026 and for 2027, based on contracts already awarded, to determine the additional allocation needed.
According to the MOF, the original allocations approved for rural road projects under the annual budgets were RM1.09 billion in 2023, RM1.32 billion in 2024 and RM1.57 billion in 2025.
“To reduce payment arrears, the KKDW took steps to reallocate existing development expenditure funds from other projects through an internal Notice of Change (NOC) to meet the funding requirements of rural projects,” it said.
The MOF said the measure resulted in the allocations being revised to RM1.85 billion in 2023, RM2.02 billion in 2024 and RM2.27 billion in 2025, but the amounts were still insufficient to cover the ministry’s project commitments.
To address the issue, the MOF said it had agreed to increase the allocations for rural road projects to RM2.11 billion in 2026 and RM2.27 billion in 2027.
Meanwhile, the ministry said the adjusted allocation for 2026 stood at RM2.40 billion, with RM2 billion in expenditure recorded as at August 31. — Bernama

Title: No decision yet on raising motorcycle licence age to 18, says Anthony Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government has yet to decide whether to raise the minimum age for obtaining a motorcycle licence.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the ministry is weighing the risk of pushing more underage riders onto the roads without valid licences.
“The proposal had been discussed years ago, but there were pros and cons to changing the current minimum age of 16.
“If you raise the age limit, secondary school students cannot get their licence. It will be a problem also, because then the student will ride motorcycles without a valid licence,” Loke told a press conference at the Transport Exhibition (TXA) here today.
He noted that some students aged 13 or 14 were already riding motorcycles without licences despite the existing minimum age.
“This is not something which is a straightforward answer. It cannot just be about increasing the age limit,” he said.
The minister said the issue needed to be considered seriously, adding that at the moment there is yet to be a decision made on changing the minimum age for motorcycle licences.
He was responding to a proposal made by the Malaysian Road Safety Research Institute (Miros), that the minimum age for obtaining motorcycle licence should be raised to 18 to help curb illegal street racing for minors.
Miros chairman Professor Wong Shaw Voon cited this as a serious issue as it involved children as young as 12 who are riding without motorcycle licences.

Title: ECRL targets Dec 12 launch with 30pc fare discount, freight services to run concurrently, says Anthony Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) will offer a 30 per cent discount on Economy Transit and Express fares for the first month of operations.
The Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) is targeting December 12 for the start of services, with ticket sales expected to begin in mid-November, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said after launching the Transport Expo Asia 2026 here today.
“The promotional discount applies to the public who do not qualify for existing concessionary fares, while eligible passengers, including persons with disabilities (OKU), children age two to 12, senior citizens and students, will continue to enjoy permanent 50 per cent discounts.
“Fares were set with affordability and the company’s financial sustainability in mind.
“We have taken a middle-ground approach,” Loke said, adding that while ECRL fares were comparable with airline tickets, they were significantly cheaper.
He also said the journey time and comfort offered by the rail service were comparable to air travel.
Freight operations to begin alongside passenger services
When asked on freight operations between Gombak and Kota Bharu, Loke said they are expected to begin alongside passenger services, allowing the railway to serve both passenger and cargo transport needs.
“Freight services connecting to Port Klang will take approximately another year to be completed, as construction of the section between Gombak and Port Klang is still ongoing.
“MRL will review freight charges in due course,” he added.
Cabinet approval on ECRL extension to Rantau Panjang
On the ECRL extension, Loke said the Cabinet has approved a proposed 32km extension Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, reaching the Malaysia-Thailand border.
“The project is now at the stage of cost and technical studies, alongside land acquisition, and is expected to take approximately four and a half years to complete.
“The first two years will focus mainly on land acquisition and technical evaluation, as land along the proposed corridor must be acquired from the state government and local landowners before construction can begin,” he said.
He added that the extension is expected to strengthen cross-border rail connectivity, although further details on its cost, construction schedule and implementation have yet to be provided.

Title: Border agency chief Shuhaily to face court tomorrow over alleged assault of two police personnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has confirmed that he will appear at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court tomorrow to face a charge of assaulting two police personnel.
Mohd Shuhaily said he was prepared to face the country’s legal process and accept whatever decision the court made in the case.
“As I have said before, bringing about changes to improve Malaysia’s borders comes at a price, and that price is myself,” he said when contacted today.
He also thanked Malaysians for their continued support as he carried out the duties entrusted to him.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was previously reported as saying that the case was being investigated by Bukit Aman’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which deals with voluntarily causing hurt.
Mohd Khalid said statements had so far been recorded from 25 witnesses to assist in the investigation into the incident, which occurred on September 28.
Mohd Shuhaily had previously left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following the circulation of a viral video showing him confronting two individuals at KLIA Terminal 1.
Meanwhile, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, when contacted, confirmed that Mohd Shuhaily would be charged with two counts under Section 323 of the Penal Code.
“I confirm that Shuhaily (Mohd Shuhaily) will be charged at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court tomorrow with two counts of causing hurt to two police personnel at the scene,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says SC pursued fresh Serba Dinamik charges under Madani, AG task force report to be made public within three months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told Parliament today that the Securities Commission (SC) pursued further action in the corporate scandal involving Serba Dinamik Berhad, leading to new charges in early 2026.
The scandal caused huge financial losses to shareholders after Serba Dinamik’s market capitalisation plunged by more than 99 per cent, from RM6 billion in early 2020 to about RM50 million by late December 2022.
Anwar said the SC had initially charged Serba Dinamik and its managing director, Datuk Mohd Abdul Karim Abdullah, in December 2021 over false statements submitted to Bursa Malaysia.
However, he claimed that under the previous administration in May 2022, the SC was directed to withdraw all charges following the payment of RM16 million in compounds, resulting in the court discharging and acquitting all the accused.
“Under the Madani administration, the SC pursued investigations into other transactions involving Datuk Karim. This action led to charges being filed against him and another individual in early 2026 regarding transactions and false statements involving Sarawak Consolidated Industries Berhad,” he said during PM Question Time.
Anwar was responding to a question on the status of investigations into allegations of a purported “corporate mafia”, which Bloomberg reported had plotted hostile takeovers of companies linked to projects that received government tenders.
Both Bloomberg investigative reports cited dozens of unnamed sources, including individuals purported to be active Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police officers.
Task force report on corporate mafia to be made public
When initially asked about the status of the probe, Anwar did not directly answer the question but later clarified that he had instructed a special task force led by the Attorney General (AG) to finalise its investigation and publicly disclose its findings within three months.
“Because this matter has arisen and I want the coordination to be more effective, I have asked the attorney general to lead a task force involving all enforcement agencies — namely MACC, PDRM, Bank Negara, SC, LHDN, and AMLA,” Anwar said.
“I have asked for a complete report so that people do not assume this lacks transparency or that someone is being protected. Let it be completed within a three-month time-frame, and because this report is not merely a civil service report but a government report, I have requested that it be disclosed to the public,” he added.
Anwar denied claims that his government was protecting anyone, pledging to make the special committee’s findings public.
“This will show that nothing is being protected. Even if names were mentioned and evidence was cited, let it come out — regardless of whether the names mentioned were Azam Baki, Farhaj, or Victor Chin, it doesn’t matter,” he said.
“Let us get full disclosure through this special committee led by the attorney general.”
